speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in each year since 2019, how many complaints relating to secondhand smoke from neighbours has the Ministry received.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask the Senior Minister of State for the data of the 900 instances last year, how many are first-time complaints and how many are repeated complaints?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, while it is increased and then decreased, I think the data still shows that pre-pandemic, and now, post-pandemic the data look like it is doubled the number of complaints.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I have asked this before, could I ask again, what is the threshold that we are looking at before we will really look into changing our policies?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards to threshold, let me first again reiterate, as I have done many times, that we take a serious view about second-hand smoke and we sympathise with every case that is affected by second-hand smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we take a multi-prong approach, both at the local level as well as at the national level.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the local level, every time there is an instance of such a case, we go down, send advisory, encourage or verbally advise the smoker, as well as look at whether enforcement can be done, if the second-hand smoke is actually emitting from the common corridor.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We continue to look at how we can improve the situation and mitigate the cases, and every case does matter to us.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, we all know that we live in a very high-rise, highly dense, highly urbanised society.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If you look at it, first, the number of residential developments, for instance, is ever increasing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we are talking about, just for HDB flats, more than a million HDB flats.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to take that in perspective, every case we take it seriously and we do sympathise with the resident.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will do whatever we can to address this, but we also need to put this in perspective and be pragmatic about it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I think that is a perspective that we should really look into.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, as I have said to the Member, we take every case seriously.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, when we take the case seriously, it means that we are also very serious.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also concerned about the outcome of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: On that serious note, order, end of question time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
